sb_prompt: FIND OUT ABOUT THE OTHER CALLER'S HOME.  IS IT A TYPICAL HOME FOR THE AREA?  HOW DOES IT COMPARE TO YOUR HOME?
raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hey!
ParticipantA: Yeah, you got the wrong number? No, wait, no, I'm actually from the list. I'm supposed to talk to people about houses.
ParticipantB: Oh, okay. Me too. That's weird.
ParticipantA: Yeah, it is. So, uh, tell me about your place. Is it like a typical house where you live?
ParticipantB: Well, I live in a little townhouse. Three floors. It's got a small kitchen and a big living room downstairs.
ParticipantA: Oh, that sounds... small. I drive trucks all day, so I don't really see that much, but I heard small places are hard to find.
ParticipantB: They are. My landlord keeps raising rent. But honestly, I think it's actually nice because I don't have to mow the lawn or fix the roof.
ParticipantA: Oh, that makes sense. I have a two-story house out in the 'burbs. Big yard, two cars.
ParticipantB: Wow. Two cars? You live in a house with two cars?
ParticipantA: Yeah. It's... it's a big house. Maybe too big? I mean, I work nights and I'm always tired, so I don't really use the second bedroom much.
ParticipantB: That's fair. Sometimes I wish my place was bigger, but then again, less cleaning is good for me too. I work restaurant service, you know?
ParticipantA: Oh, right. I see. I worked in a restaurant once for a summer, actually. It was crazy.
ParticipantB: Really? What was it like?
ParticipantA: It was loud. And fast. One night I spilled coffee on a guy's pants and he got really mad. I felt bad for a long time.
ParticipantB: Oh, man. I spilled red wine on a tablecloth last week. The whole table got it. The customers didn't say anything, but my manager did.
ParticipantA: Yeah, that sucks. I felt like I wanted to quit that job. It was just... stressful.
ParticipantB: I feel that way sometimes. But I keep coming back because I like the people. You know?
ParticipantA: I guess so. Though my house is quieter. At least I can just sit on the porch and listen to the birds. No screaming kids or loud servers.
ParticipantB: That sounds nice. A quiet porch. Do you ever feel like your house is too quiet though? Sometimes I get lonely in my apartment.
ParticipantA: Sometimes. Yeah, actually. Last week I invited a couple friends over and we just talked for hours. It was nice.
ParticipantB: Oh, that's sweet. Do you do that often?
ParticipantA: Not really. I'm usually too tired after being on the road. But yeah, it felt good.
ParticipantB: I guess I'm in the middle. I like my small place, but I wish it was bigger. And I like the people, but the job is exhausting.
ParticipantA: Yeah, that's exactly how I feel. It's a bit of a trap sometimes. You get used to it.
ParticipantB: Exactly. So is your house typical for the area? I mean, are most people here living in big houses?
ParticipantA: Yeah, mostly. Most people around here have big yards. But my neighbors have a lot of older cars.
ParticipantB: Oh, really? Older cars? I have a brand new car, but it's small. Maybe I'll need a bigger one soon.
ParticipantA: Maybe. My truck is an older one, but it gets me around.
ParticipantB: Yeah, trucks are great. I'm jealous of the space.
ParticipantA: Well, you never know. Maybe you'll buy a bigger place eventually.
ParticipantB: Maybe. Or maybe I'll stay here and just enjoy the porch.
ParticipantA: Yeah, sounds good. Thanks for telling me about it.
ParticipantB: Yeah, same to you. It was nice talking.
ParticipantA: Yep. Bye.
ParticipantB: Bye.
